style_when: the article describes one decisive moment or place — a yard at dawn, a control room, a shutdown line, a handover — that a film still could hold
prompt: Wide 35mm anamorphic photograph inside a dark data hall. A brushed steel security gate blocks a rack aisle; one fiber-optic cable carrying a warm white data stream passes through a narrow vertical slot into an allowed server bay. A blank yellow plastic permit tag hangs from the latch. Hard directional light from high left rakes across the perforated metal gate, long shadows; graphite, steel blue and amber. Asymmetric composition, hero gate off-centre right, generous negative space left, shallow depth of field, fine film grain, no people, no text, no logos.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, watermarks, legible words
rationale: This is a systemic software security story, not a single artifact, so cinematic_still frames the checkpoint as a decisive moment in the data hall. The steel gate and fiber cable make the allowed-address trust line tangible while the hard directional light gives it editorial weight.
subject: a permitted fiber-optic cable passing through a locked steel security gate in a data hall
core_thesis: The MCP trust line is the data each call carries, not the publisher's signature or the list of allowed addresses, and holding that line costs less than resetting the tool between calls.
core_conflict: signature and destination allowlist authorization versus call-carried data persistence
composition: extreme asymmetry, gate off-centre right with generous negative space left

review.depicts: A dark data-hall aisle lined with server cabinets receding to the left, while in the right foreground a warm-glowing cable arcs out of a port on a perforated metal server panel and hangs past a small blank amber tag.
review.reason: The frame shows an authorized, tagged connection inside a data hall — the article's own object, a permitted path still carrying data outward — rather than an unrelated industry or generic filler.
